summary: The cast has strong toy-like proportions, useful silhouette variety and readable close-shot jokes, but several costumes still read as modern uniforms or superhero capes rather than constructed Stone Age clothing. The board's approval note does not resolve the Chief's prohibited ceremonial sash, Kit's conflicting gold badge, or the loss of identification in the free-play greyscale check.
problems: Kit's blue outfit reads as a matching manufactured uniform, and his gold badge assigns the Chief's story colour to a member of Wren's band; replace the badge with bone and rebuild the outfit as visibly tied hide.

The Chief wears a broad diagonal sash with a medal-like knot despite the bible explicitly excluding modern mayoral sashes; move his gold identity onto an irregular layered hide mantle and rawhide bindings.
The actual-size free-play greyscale strip does not reliably distinguish Wren from Kit without lineup position; strengthen their silhouettes and value separation before passing the phone gate.
Wren's rigid red shoulder slabs and straight cape panels suggest superhero clothing; retain her dominant red mass but express it through overlapping hide, irregular hems and visible ties.
Oak's rectangular orange apron and exceptionally regular mallet head look manufactured; introduce hide construction and a rough, visibly lashed stone tool head without losing his broad silhouette.
Ash's rear cape is a large straight-edged slab; replace it with uneven overlapping hide panels and a clearly supported shoulder fastening.
Matching blue torso, cape and footwear read as a uniform rather than gathered and tied Stone Age clothing.
The gold chest badge conflicts with his membership in Wren's band.
His small dark silhouette becomes too similar to Wren's in free-play greyscale.
elements.fix: Keep blue as one hide-wrap mass, expose neutral hide boots and sinew closures, and replace the gold badge with an unpainted bone token. Give his imitation staff a thicker, offset silhouette that remains separate from his torso at actual phone size.

problems: The diagonal gold sash and oversized round knot reproduce modern civic regalia.
The mantle reads as stacked rectangular shoulder armour rather than layered hide.
The headdress has antler-like branches but no clearly readable feather component.
elements.fix: Remove the sash geometry while retaining story gold as ochre-painted areas on a broad, asymmetrically layered hide mantle and its ties. Add one chunky off-centre feather, preserve the oversized bone staff, and retain an absurdly excessive hide fastening as the vanity joke.

problems: Close-shot recognition is substantially stronger than free-play recognition.
At free-play size, Wren and Kit rely heavily on relative height and lineup position.
Oak's mid-value clothing has weak separation from the dirt; a proposed future outline is not evidence of a current pass.
elements.fix: Strengthen distinguishing outer contours and introduce broad light-dark breaks within each existing four-colour palette. Re-render the 390 px greyscale check with shuffled positions and representative town clutter; include any intended outline in the actual render.

problems: The squared shoulder assembly and rigid flared cape read closer to superhero costume construction than tied hide.
Her top-knot helps at close range but does not sufficiently separate her from Kit at free-play size.
elements.fix: Preserve the dominant story-red upper body and tally stick, but replace the shoulder slabs with two overlapping hide flaps, one visible bone fastening and an asymmetric cape hem. Make one side of the wrap project clearly enough to distinguish her contour in greyscale.

problems: The orange apron is an almost perfectly rectangular plate with ruler-straight edges.
The mallet's regular pale block and neat central band suggest a manufactured hammer.
elements.fix: Give the apron a folded upper edge, unequal lower corners and chunky rawhide neck and waist ties. Reshape the mallet into an asymmetric faceted stone with crossed lashings around a crooked wooden haft, keeping its head clear of his silhouette.

problems: The back view exposes a broad, flat, straight-edged grey cape with little evidence of hide construction.
The rigid pale collar reinforces an armour-like reading.
elements.fix: Break the cape into two unequal overlapping hides with a stepped torn edge and a visible shoulder tie. Replace the continuous pale collar with interrupted fur masses, preserving his tall frame and oversized bandage-knot joke.
